title: Letter of respondent United States notifying the Court that the government will be filing a merits brief in support of the petitioner on the question presented,

pages.text:
U.S. Department of Justice
Office of the Solicitor General

The Solicitor General     Washington, D.C. 20530


       May 12, 2025

Honorable Scott S. Harris
Clerk
Supreme Court of the United States
Washington, D.C. 20543

Re:  Ellingburg v. United States , No. 24-482
Dear Mr. Harris:
The Court granted certiorari in this case on April 7, 2025.  In opposing certiorari, the government did not express a position about the correctness of the rationale of the court of appeals’
opinion.  The government instead contended that the court of appeals’ judgment should be affirmed
because, even assuming that restitution ordered pursuant to the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act
of 1996 (MVRA) is a criminal penalty, retroactively applying the statutory amendment that petitioner challenges did not result in an increase in punishment that would violate the Ex Post  Facto
Clause.
The purpose of this letter is to notify the Court that the Solicitor General has determined
that government will not defend the rationale of the court of appeals’ decision.  The government
will file a brief in support of petitioner on the question presente d, which is limited to whether
restitution under the MVRA is criminal punishment for purposes of the Ex Post Facto Clause.
Although the government continues to believe that there is no Ex Post Facto Clause violation in
this case and that the judgment of t he court of appeals should ultimately be sustained, its reasons
are beyond the scope of the question on which the Court has granted review.
The government intends to file its brief on the deadline for petitioner’s brief on the merits,
and it joins petitioner’s request for an extension of that deadline to June 23, 2025.
Under the circumstances, the Court may wish to invite an amicus curiae to file a brief to
defend the rationale of the court of appeals’ decision.

       Sincerely,



       D. John Sauer
       Solicitor General
